title: systemd journal (persistent)
whyItMatters: The persistent systemd journal records services started, logins, errors and device events across reboots. It builds a timeline of how the machine was used, long after the plain log files were rotated away.
source: systemd-journald docs: with Storage=persistent the journal is kept in /var/log/journal, otherwise it lives only in /run: https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemd-journald.service.html
notes: Sizes only; the journal files themselves are normally root-only or readable by the systemd-journal and adm groups, so a normal user gets permission skips. When Storage=volatile the folder does not exist and the journal is lost at shutdown. Individual user journals under ~/.local/share are not covered.
